## 10th Frame: A Bowling Simulation for the Ages

Step onto the lanes with *10th Frame*, a realistic ten-pin bowling simulation released in 1986 for the Commodore 64 and other platforms. This sports game, developed by Access Software and published by U.S. Gold, allows up to eight players to compete in either "Open Bowling" or "League" modes. Tailor the challenge to your skill level by selecting individual player abilities – Kids, Amateur, or Professional – ensuring a fun and competitive experience for everyone.

Gameplay revolves around precise aiming and timing. Before each throw, players can adjust their position on the lane and utilize a unique power meter, similar to *Leaderboard*, to control the speed and spin of the ball. Mastering the hook zone is key to achieving strikes and spares. With detailed animation and realistic pin physics, *10th Frame* delivers an immersive bowling experience. Computer Gaming World even hailed it as one of their top 10 sports games of all time, praising its slick programming and addictive gameplay. Prepare to test your skills and become a bowling champion!

The Commodore 64, affectionately known as the C64, was an 8-bit home computer released in 1982 that became a cultural icon and the best-selling desktop computer of all time, with estimated sales between 12.5 and 17 million units. Boasting 64 kilobytes of RAM and impressive graphics and sound capabilities thanks to its VIC-II chip and SID sound chip, the C64 offered a significant leap in performance compared to its predecessors. It initially sold for $595, but its price later dropped, making it accessible to a wider audience.

The C64 dominated the home computer market throughout the 1980s, particularly in the US and UK, though it faced stiff competition from the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC. Popular games like *Impossible Mission*, *The Last Ninja*, and *Elite* showcased its capabilities and cemented its legacy. Even today, emulators allow enthusiasts to relive the C64 experience.
